issues.quote: The sage took her far away.
issues.problem: A1 never says the sage took the horse. Later the prince is with 'the horse' in another land and says 'Bring the horse outside,' so the reader cannot tell how the horse got there.
issues.fix: The sage put her on the horse and flew far away.

issues.quote: He turned a small part on its side.
issues.problem: 'Turned a small part' is vague and unnatural. A learner cannot picture what was turned. The same issue appears in 'Then the young man found a second part.'
issues.fix: He turned a small key on its side. / Then the young man found a second key. (A2 already uses 'key'.)

issues.quote: In one room, he found a young girl. She was the princess of Sana.
issues.problem: Calling her 'a young girl' and then saying they were in love after a night in her room is uncomfortable for a 4+ app. It also clashes with the other levels, which say 'young woman'.
issues.fix: In one room, he found a young woman. She was the princess of Sana.

notes: 'The horse came down on a big house' would read more naturally as 'on top of a big house' (as A2 has it).
'The sage did not show the way down' could be 'The sage did not tell him how to go down.'
'Bring the horse outside' has no reason given. A short reason such as 'The horse can help her' would make the doctor trick clearer, but this is optional.
'There, a king saw them and took the princess home.' 'Home' could be read as the princess's home. 'Took the princess to his palace' is clearer.
'The young prince did not like this plan': nobody made a plan. 'did not like this' or 'was angry' is better.
'Bring her and the horse into the open field': no field was mentioned before, so 'a field' fits better.
'In the morning, her father found them together' is acceptable, but 'found the young man in her room' avoids any innuendo.

issues.quote: In the morning, a servant saw the stranger and ran to the king of Sana. "Who is this man in my daughter's room?" he demanded. "I am the son of the king of Persia, and I love your daughter," he replied.
issues.problem: Both 'he's point back to the servant, the last subject named, and the king is never shown arriving. A reader stumbles over who demands and who replies.
issues.fix: The king hurried to the room. "Who is this man in my daughter's room?" the king demanded. "I am the son of the king of Persia, and I love your daughter," the prince replied.

notes: 'Far above the earth, the prince understood the sage's trick. At last, he found a second peg on its left shoulder.' 'Its' follows 'trick', so 'on the horse's left shoulder' is clearer.

In the original the first sage's gift is the trumpet (held by a golden figure) and the second is the peacock. B1, B2 and C1 swap the order, and the B1 quiz asks about the 'first' gift. This is minor, but swapping the order back (and the quiz key with it) would be more faithful.

issues.quote: The prince left the princess there to rest, because he wanted to ride ahead and arrange a proper welcome for her.
issues.problem: The only horse in the story is the ebony horse. If he 'rode ahead', the horse would be gone, yet in the next sentences the sage finds 'the princess and the ebony horse' and flies off on it. In the original the prince leaves the horse with her and goes into the city.
issues.fix: The prince left the princess and the horse there to rest, because he wanted to go ahead into the city and arrange a proper welcome for her.

notes: 'When she woke and saw a stranger beside her' sounds like he was in the bed with her. For a 4+ app, 'saw a stranger standing near her bed' is safer.
Gift order is reversed compared with the original (see the B1 note).

issues.quote: A small summer pavilion stood there among the trees, and he rode ahead to prepare a fitting welcome.
issues.problem: This has the same contradiction as B2. He 'rode ahead', yet the sage then sees 'the ebony horse and the beautiful stranger beside it' and flies away on it.
issues.fix: A small summer pavilion stood there among the trees, and leaving the horse beside her, he went ahead on foot to prepare a fitting welcome.

notes: The prose is genuinely literary and faithful otherwise. 'An entire army was left staring at an empty sky' and the 'one captor for another' line are strong.
Gift order is reversed compared with the original (see the B1 note).

summary: The retelling is faithful to the Arabian Nights tale, age-appropriate on the whole, and well matched to each level, and all quizzes are keyed correctly. It fails on small logic problems: A1 never says the sage took the horse, B1 has an unclear speaker in the Sana confrontation, and B2/C1 say the prince 'rode ahead' while the ebony horse stays in the garden. A1 also needs 'part' replaced and 'young girl' changed to 'young woman'.
